easy.def: To decide who or what is best.
examples: My teacher will judge the art show.
Do not judge a book by its cover.
Who will judge the pie contest?

more.def: To form an opinion about something, or to decide the winner of a contest.
examples: Three chefs judged the baking contest.
It is hard to judge how far away the mountain is.
You should not judge people by their clothes.
The orange is sweet and juicy.
We ate juicy watermelon.
The pear is ripe and juicy.
He bit into a ripe, juicy peach.
The grill made the chicken tender and juicy.
Bees buzzed around the juicy plums on the ground.

easy.def: A hot place with lots of trees and plants.
examples: Monkeys live in the jungle.
A snake hides in the jungle.
The jungle is wet and green.

more.def: A thick forest in a hot, rainy part of the world.
examples: Bright parrots flew through the jungle.
Explorers cut a path through the thick jungle.
The jungle was noisy with the calls of birds and frogs.

easy.def: Only, or a very short time ago.
examples: I want just one cookie.
We just got home.
It is just a little bug.

more.def: Only or simply, or a very short time before now.
examples: There is just enough paint left to finish the fence.
The bell just rang, so the class is over.
I am just going to rest for a minute.
Justice means the rules are fair for all.
The judge wants justice.
Heroes in stories fight for justice.

more.def: Fair treatment for everyone, following what is right.
examples: The judge worked hard to make sure there was justice.
The people marched to ask for justice.
A fair trial is an important part of justice.
